selected_generation.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit with identity preservation.
Asset type: Akari v3.1 slim-hairpin color/material exploration.
Primary request: Recolor ONLY the existing blue hairpin in Image 1 to the silver-family finish specified below.

Input roles:
Image 1 is candidate A, the sole edit target. Preserve its exact composition, existing slim pin geometry, rounded ends, length, thickness, tilt, attachment, and position on the viewer-right temple above the visible ear. It is the authority for every non-pin part of the image.
Image 2 is P1, supporting reference only for the already established original facial identity, rounded grey downturned eyes, cheeks, black bob, segmented bangs and drawing treatment. Do not copy its open mouth.
Image 3 is P2, supporting reference only for the existing closed-mouth everyday smile, shirt and leafy setting. It does not authorize removing the pin.

Keep the face, both eye shapes and iris highlights, brow lines, nose, closed-mouth smile, fine cheek hatching, skin shading, round black bob silhouette, all bangs and hair highlights, neck, white short-sleeve open-collar shirt with blue-grey piping, pose, skirt, leafy outdoor background, lighting, square 1254x1254 framing and drawing style unchanged. No character redesign or age-based change. The single pin remains the same plain, very slim, straight bar. Do not enlarge or thicken it, bend it, move it, turn it into a loop or triangle, or add a second pin. No text, label, grid, border, watermark, jewelry or other ornament.
Edit only the blue color and surface reflectance of that existing hairpin. Fit the metal shading to the original soft daylight and illustrated rendering, keeping highlights within the current pin silhouette.
Target finish: Bright neutral-cool polished silver. A light silver-grey metallic body, one restrained narrow near-white daylight reflection, and a thin soft darker-grey edge to describe the metal. Clearly brighter than the hair and legible at normal viewing size, but no glowing white, glitter, lens flare or jewel-like sparkle. Remove the former periwinkle-blue enamel hue completely.
